correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the facet areas by clipping octant triangles and coordinate squares/diamonds. For x≥y≥z≥0, Cauchy's sum reduces to 4(x+y+z+(x−y−z)_+). The two linear functionals on the resulting cones give the upper bounds by Cauchy–Schwarz, with the tilted vector feasible at and above b/a=2/3. In the balanced cone, 1≤xS≤S²/2 gives the lower bound with equality only at a face diagonal; in the dominant cone, normalize its three extreme rays and use strictness of the triangle inequality for mixtures. This gives the axis/face-diagonal crossing at b/a=√2−1. The derivative of b/a is negative on both open chambers; the radicals and orbit counts follow. At c=3 the two upper-bound expressions also coincide (b=0), but the candidate tilted/body-diagonal vector is not in the dominant cone; the proof's phrase about both orbits surviving applies only to the interior crossing. Directly B=4S at c=3, so the Finding's endpoint classification is correct. An independently written finite comparison of candidate values and ratios also passed; the all-direction and equality claims use the analytic proof, not sampling.

evidence: The October spectral theorem computes the even facet-network spectrum and uses m_F=h_F area(F). Dividing its displayed diagonal and coordinate masses by c/√3 and 1 gives this record's two face-area formulas. Its crossing (7+√13)/6 concerns an eigenvalue, not brightness. Catalog claims 20022a556c31 and 9ba1a511dacf concern illumination number and inscribed tetrahedron volume, respectively.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Neither a facet mass nor a spectral extremum is an extremum of the projection-body support. Cauchy's formula yields the brightness profile from the masses, but optimizing it over both cones with all equality cases is additional work.

originality.rationale: Known ingredients and fixed-body cases are not credited as new. The strongest matching indexed record genuinely duplicates both open-chamber transitions, including the maximizing and minimizing equality sets, but is indexed in November, after this frozen October record. It adds plateau/design discussion and does not cover the second chamber or endpoints. It is not evidence of antecedent coverage. The earlier same-family spectral theorem supplies the face areas, not the angular optimization. No inspected antecedent establishes the full claimed classification; this is not a claim of absolute priority.
residual_risks: The earlier regular truncated-octahedron citation 9442beb3-c40f-4055-88e9-2d5874e8e7af and the Abas full text were not recovered. The exact indexed November overlap fixes no absolute publication-priority claim. An uninspected general projection-body result or differently indexed family analysis could cover more.
